title: RNA-sequencing of meningiomas for integrative molecular classification

publications.title: A clinically applicable integrative molecular classification of meningiomas.

needs_manual_review_reason: NEW RECORD (2026-07-11), found via an author/lab-based search (Nassiri F publication list), never previously found by keyword search since it is EGA-hosted (controlled access) rather than in GEO. This is bulk RNA-seq data for the same Nassiri et al. 2021 Nature integrative-classification cohort already represented in this inventory via mng-utoronto-2021-genomic.json (cBioPortal: CNV/mutation/proteomics) and gse-180061-methylation.json (methylation, the canonical record of a confirmed duplicate pair with gse-168726-methylation.json). That cBioPortal record's own needs_manual_review_reason explicitly notes that despite the study description mentioning 'RNA abundance,' zero RNA-seq samples were actually loaded into cBioPortal, this EGA dataset is that missing RNA-seq data, hosted separately. Verified directly via the EGA Metadata API: study EGAS00001004982 ('Integrative Molecular Classification of Meningiomas', exact title match to the published paper), dataset EGAD00001007494 ('RNA-sequencing of meningiomas for integrative molecular classification'), 124 samples, released 2001-01-01 placeholder date in the EGA record (not a real release date, EGA sometimes uses this as a default/unset value; treated as 'Not reported' rather than taken literally). A third dataset in the same study, EGAD00001007051 (whole-exome sequencing, 184 tumor/normal pairs), is lower priority as a 'new' finding since cBioPortal's mng_utoronto_2021 record already exposes processed mutation calls derived from this same exome data (115 samples with sequencing-based calls); listed in related_accessions but not extracted as its own record. paired_multimodal.related_datasets links to the companion snRNA-seq record (egad00001007677-nassiri-snrnaseq), the cBioPortal record, and the canonical methylation record; gse-180061-methylation.json's own paired_multimodal has been updated to reference back. Only public EGA study/dataset-level metadata was used; the controlled-access sequencing data itself was never accessed, per docs/scope.md's compliance guardrail. FACT-CHECK UPDATE 2026-07-11: platform was wrong, corrected from 'Not reported' to 'Illumina HiSeq 2500'. This was already present in the live EGA dataset record (https://metadata.ega-archive.org/datasets/EGAD00001007494 returns technologies:['Illumina HiSeq 2500']), one of this record's own cited source_urls, but had not been copied into the platform field by the prior extraction; no new source was needed, just re-reading the already-cited API response. CROSS-LINK ADDED (2026-07-13): msv000086901-nassiri-proteomics.json (this paper's proteomics arm, MassIVE MSV000086901) added as a new record and cross-linked here. DEEP-AUDIT FIX (2026-07-14): publications[0].authors was truncated to 6 of the paper's 26 authors (Europe PMC authorString for PMID 34433969 confirmed the full list ending 'Boutros PC, Bader GD, de Carvalho DD, Kislinger T, Aldape K, Zadeh G.'); expanded to all 26. corresponding_author changed from 'Farshad Nassiri / Gelareh Zadeh' to 'Gelareh Zadeh': fetched the live Nature/PMC full text (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11604310/, raw HTML) and found exactly one author-notes footnote (id=CR1) marked with a single ✉ symbol reading verbatim 'Correspondence should be addressed to: Gelareh Zadeh, MD, PhD, Division of Neurosurgery, University of Toronto, MacFeeters Hamilton Neuro-Oncology Program, Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, University, Health Network, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, gelareh.zadeh@uhn.ca'; Nassiri is not named there. (Separately, Aldape and Zadeh both carry a '**' superscript, but that footnote reads only 'These authors contributed equally', an equal-contribution marker distinct from corresponding authorship -- not a second correspondence designation.) grade_breakdown/brain_invasion/treatment_timepoint_status/has_outcome_data re-checked against the same full text: confirms grading was WHO-2016 with 'tumors spanning all WHO grades... in each molecular group' but no per-sample breakdown specific to the 124 RNA-seq samples, and brain invasion is not among the paper's listed clinical data elements; all left as 'Not reported'/null, no change.
